steps.claim: replay09 checks only p.signature() != f.signature(). That includes internal bounds but omits borrowed lifetime requirements. It then executes the expected program with the subject's same Invocation, whose borrowed_widths came only from f; execute_element_bound uses that inventory even when f is the expected function.

In fixed-image-incompatible.bisa, lookup is the unchanged controlled-dirty subject with inventory [1]. Added clean has the identical signature and qload/cx/qunload body but no qborrow or cancelling borrowed CX pair, hence inventory []. The claim expects clean at args=[], budget=[0,0,0,0], fixed image 0102 and one inherited control. Parse and check_hashes succeed, and both checker APIs incorrectly return ProofRelativeToImage with n=256, |D|=16777216 and fraction=1/65536. The required outcome is rejection for incompatible borrowed interfaces. The smaller incompatible-empty.bisa likewise returns unrestricted Proof for [1] versus [], and incompatible-narrower.bisa returns Proof for [2] versus [1].

Conversely, compatible-different-bounds.bisa compares a(t)={qloop 2 {x t; x t}} with z(t)={x t; x t}. Both have one mutable bit, no other slots/arguments/borrows and identity semantics. The full t=0..1 domain with args=[] and zero budget must give Proof, n=|D|=2. Both APIs instead reject with 'expected program has an incompatible signature' because bounds [2] differs from [].

The compatibility predicate is simultaneously too weak for borrowed interfaces and too strict for legal source bodies. The fixed-image proof in step <1>3 is issued for a relation that fails the mandated interface precondition, while step <1>4 rejects a legal relation. These are S0 divergences, not an optional implementation restriction or an ambiguity.
